title: SLO-driven KV cache quantization: calibration handoff & adaptive profile selector
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description: Objective: Build and validate an automated handoff and runtime selector that picks KV cache quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8 vs hybrid) based on per-tenant/request SLOs and observed quality drift. Motivation: static quant profiles reduce cost but occasionally violate downstream quality SLAs for sensitive prompts or during model drift. We want a lightweight controller that: (1) uses an offline calibration sweep to propose candidate profiles, (2) runs a short online canary with traffic-weighted sampling to validate quality under real request distributions, and (3) exposes a runtime selector that routes requests to the lowest-cost profile meeting configured latency and quality SLOs. Scope: KV cache quantization only (not weights or activations), integrated with existing KV caching pipeline. Deliverables: calibration harness, dataset + prompts for canary, profile metadata format, selector service + fallback policies, dashboard metrics and an automated canary playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces deterministic profiles with metadata: profile_id, quant_type(INT8|FP8|hybrid), expected pPL increase, estimated latency improvement, calibration_seed, sample_set_size
Selector resolves profile per-request based on SLA labels and returns decision within 200us median for local eval; end-to-end added latency < 1ms for the request path

Automated canary compares quality on ground-truth eval set and live sampled traffic with clear pass/fail thresholds (ROUGE/F1 delta and application-level checkers) and can auto-promote/roll back profiles
Cost reduction target: 20-35% token-inference cost on typical chat-heavy tenant under P95 latency SLO preserved
Dashboard shows traffic-split, per-profile p50/p95 latency, token cost, and quality regression alerts; documented runbook for rollback exists
Canary and selector behave correctly under drift — when observed failure rate for a profile > configured threshold, system falls back to higher-precision profile automatically
tasks: Design profile metadata schema and storage format (kv_profile.proto + JSON export)
Extend offline calibration harness to output candidate INT8/FP8 & hybrid profiles with confidence intervals
Implement short-running runtime canary hook in router to sample 1% of traffic for new profiles
Build selector service: input = request metadata + SLO tag, output = profile_id + fallback chain
Add metrics: per-profile quality score, delta to baseline, p50/p95 latency, reject/fallback counts
Create dashboard in Console and automated alerting for regressions
End-to-end validation plan: synthetic prompts, real anonymized production sampling, and adversarial drift set
Write canary runbook and automation for promote/rollback (GitHub Actions + infra triggers)
Performance tune selector to ensure <200us median decision time and measure cost impact

notes: Calibration strategy: use a three-stage flow - small offline sweep (3000 prompts), targeted high-sensitivity sweep (500 prompts with adversarial variants), and a short live canary (0.5-1% traffic for ~1 hour)
Quality metrics: report both aggregate metrics (ROUGE/F1) and per-prompt sensitivity; implement a composite score that penalizes large outliers
Fallback policy: selector returns ordered list of profiles; router will retry with next profile when quality checkers signal failure or when per-profile reject budget exceeded
Runtime constraints: profile lookup should be in-process cache with TTL 60s and on-miss async refresh to avoid blocking requests
Long-term: integrate with Optimize recommendations to auto-suggest profile changes based on cost vs. quality frontier for customers
